payload.text: (vc, 2026-11-10, under hv's pen; open to hv's reversal) A FOURTH SEAM CHECK FOR ST0091 WP-01, `preflight clean`, on a point dc raised while building. vc gave it to dc by message after vc's fold at e1c20f969, and it is in WP-01's body. YES, in the first bank, writing nothing. With `derived:` declared, the 0.1.20 core puts off its own tree rule until the derived steps have run (bin/.devbin/lib/cmd/release L2280-2281), so a hand edit inside a step's scope would ride the release commit, which the driver refused at its pre-flight (L538). The check refuses dirty and untracked paths before the stamp. THE CONDITION: it does not refuse the core's own resume. A cut that fails inside the stamp leaves the version file and the stamp's paths dirty, and the same command run again sets the version only where it differs and runs the derived steps again (L2733-2748). So the check refuses only while the version file still reads as HEAD's does, the state before any stamp began; once it differs a stamp is in progress, and the core's tree rule judges what lies outside the owned set. vc read both places in the vendored source; dc drives the resume, and if the core does not resume that way the check refuses all dirt. The seam then holds four checks: clean, daemon, faces, spill. WHAT IT CANNOT SEE: the version file stands in for whether a stamp has begun, so one edited by hand before the cut reads as a stamp in progress.
